rows.who: State public utility commission (called a public service commission in some states)
rows.controls: Approves retail rates and capital spending recovery for investor-owned electric and gas utilities, divides costs among customer classes, approves special contracts and large-load tariffs; in some states also sets investor-owned water rates.
rows.how_to_reach: File a public comment or speak at a public hearing in the rate case docket; open dockets and hearing schedules are posted on the commission's website, which your state government's official site links.

rows.controls: Writes the laws that define the commission's powers, can require protections for existing customers when large loads connect, and can fund state bill assistance.
rows.how_to_reach: Contact your state senator and representative through the legislature's official website; testify at committee hearings on energy bills.

rows.who: City council or municipal utility board
rows.controls: Sets rates and spending for public power and city-owned water utilities.
rows.how_to_reach: Public comment at council or utility board meetings; agendas are posted by the city clerk or utility.

rows.controls: Sets rates and investment plans for a member-owned cooperative.
rows.how_to_reach: Attend the co-op's annual membership meeting and board meetings; bylaws and board election notices come from the co-op.

rows.controls: Approves wholesale market rules, including PJM's capacity auction design and price limits, and sets transmission revenue requirements.
rows.how_to_reach: Submit comments in the relevant docket through eComment on ferc.gov.

rows.who: PJM Interconnection and other regional grid operators
rows.controls: Forecast demand, run capacity auctions and plan transmission; rule changes must be filed with and approved by FERC.
rows.how_to_reach: Auction results, load forecasts and committee meeting materials are posted at pjm.com; formal rule changes can be commented on in FERC dockets.

rows.who: Congress and the Department of Health and Human Services
rows.controls: Congress appropriates LIHEAP funds and amends the Federal Power Act; HHS distributes LIHEAP grants to states, tribes and territories.
rows.how_to_reach: Contact your U.S. representative and senators through house.gov and senate.gov; appropriations for LIHEAP go through the Labor-HHS subcommittees.

rows.controls: Proposes rates, capital plans and contracts with large customers, and decides when to file a rate case.
rows.how_to_reach: Customer service for billing disputes; the utility's filings are public in the commission docket.
